c.tagline: A Welsh-founded Patagonian coastal town, launchpad for southern right whales and penguin colonies on Peninsula Valdes

card: Widely accepted; cash (preferably USD for exchange) useful for smaller shops

taxi.fareNote: Most visitors book an organized tour rather than a taxi for Peninsula Valdes given the distances

emergency.note: 911 is the general emergency line in most of Argentina; 107 specifically reaches medical services

religion: Protestant, including a historic Welsh Chapel community (minority)
walk: The waterfront Rambla and downtown are walkable; Peninsula Valdes and Punta Tombo require a car or organized tour given the distances involved

safety.safety: Very safe city, popular as a base for Patagonian wildlife excursions

hood_landmark.Downtown: Downtown's main commercial streets around Avenida Roca
hood_landmark.Peninsula Valdes (day-trip): Peninsula Valdes's whale-watching and wildlife viewing points
hood_landmark.El Doradillo Beach: El Doradillo Beach's shore-based whale watching
hood_landmark.Punta Tombo (day-trip): Punta Tombo's vast Magellanic penguin colony

hood_desc: The scenic beachfront promenade with hotels, restaurants, and views over the Golfo Nuevo; the natural base for any visit.
The compact commercial core a short walk inland, with everyday shops, tour agencies, and dive shops.
A UNESCO-listed wildlife peninsula a couple hours' drive away, essential for seeing whales, sea lions, and elephant seals up close.
A stretch of coastline just north of town where southern right whales can be seen remarkably close to shore in season.
A large Magellanic penguin colony south of town, best visited September through April when the birds are present.

water.note: Tap water is safe though mineral-tasting; many opt for bottled.

transit.map: Not centrally published; tour agencies handle Peninsula Valdes and Punta Tombo excursions
transit.note: A rental car or organized tour is necessary for Peninsula Valdes and Punta Tombo given the distances

transport.air: El Tehuelche Airport (PMY), about 10 min from downtown
transport.bus: Long-distance buses connect to Buenos Aires (about 18-20 hr), Bariloche, and Trelew
transport.car: Rental cars available; National Route 3 connects Puerto Madryn to the rest of coastal Patagonia

net.m: Good 4G coverage in town, patchier on Peninsula Valdes
net.w: Free wifi standard in hotels and cafes
net.ap: A Movistar, Claro, or Personal tourist SIM or eSIM
